title: CEO Interview Greene Tweed - Semiwiki
gist: In a SemiWiki CEO interview, Greene Tweed CEO Magen Buterbaugh describes how the 160-year-old family-owned materials firm sells Chemraz FFKM seals into semiconductor etch, ECD and CMP, and sees new sealing demands from AI-driven advanced packaging (hybrid bonding, glass substrates, co-packaged optics). It is expanding in Korea and Taiwan for supply resilience.

themes.theme: Advanced packaging as new sealing demand

insights.claim: AI-driven advanced packaging, including hybrid bonding, glass substrates, panel-level packaging and co-packaged optics, creates larger form factors, multi-die systems and unprecedented cleanliness requirements, opening new sealing challenges.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Packaging buildout drives demand for specialty consumables beyond wafer-fab tools, a second-order AI supply chain beneficiary.

insights.claim: With glass substrates seals must cover much larger surface areas where warpage and shifting mechanical stresses matter, and in co-packaged optics even trace outgassing can compromise optical clarity.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Material purity and outgassing specs are technical barriers favoring qualified high-end seal suppliers.

insights.claim: Greene Tweed's Chemraz FFKM seals address plasma resistance and low particulation in etch, aggressive plating acids in ECD, and abrasive slurries in CMP, where traditional elastomers struggle.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Consumable seals are recurring-revenue content tied to wafer-fab utilization and process complexity.

insights.claim: As chip architectures grow more complex, manufacturing processes involve more aggressive chemistries and higher temperatures, while fabs focus on reliability, contamination control, productivity and yield.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Process complexity raises materials content per wafer, supporting specialty materials suppliers.
insights.locator: In semiconductor, our customers are being asked

insights.claim: Greene Tweed seals are used across etch, deposition, cleaning and stripping, ECD, advanced packaging, CMP, lithography and subfab systems.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Broad process coverage indicates exposure to overall WFE activity.

insights.claim: Customers' top concern is reliability, then yield, contamination, equipment uptime, supply-chain resilience, speed of innovation and increasingly sustainability.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Qualification and reliability create switching costs for incumbent suppliers.
insights.quote: Reliability. For semiconductor customers, even the smallest component can have an outsized impact.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Greene Tweed sells predominantly direct, with engineering teams working with customers early on performance challenges.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Direct, early design-in relationships are a moat in engineered components.

insights.claim: The company is investing in supply resilience with a new facility in Korea, expanded production in Taiwan and supply from multiple US sites.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Capacity placed near Korean and Taiwanese fabs mirrors where WFE demand is concentrated.

insights.claim: Greene Tweed is a 160-plus-year-old, fourth-generation family-owned firm serving semiconductor, aerospace and defense, energy, industrial and life sciences markets, and Magen Buterbaugh became CEO in January 2023.
insights.speaker: Magen Buterbaugh
insights.so_what: Privately held, so no direct public-market exposure, but a reference for private suppliers inside the semi supply chain.
